research_problem: Knowledge on testing microservice-based architectures is fragmented across studies focusing on single levels or objectives; existing secondary studies are outdated, shallow or narrow
technical_approach: SLR: Google Scholar ALLINTITLE query (186) + Scopus (278, subset), 4-author selection (Fleiss kappa 0.78 on 25), bidirectional snowballing to saturation; SWEBOK (level, objective, strategy, type), ISO/IEC 25010, Stol-Fitzgerald study types, TRL and SUT analysis
primary_contribution: Classification of 74 microservice testing studies with 4W1H analysis, maturity (TRL) and SUT landscape, plus research directions
dataset_benchmark: 74 peer-reviewed primary studies (2015-2024); replication package Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16941552
evaluation_metrics: Descriptive counts and percentages; Fleiss kappa for selection agreement
baselines: Prior secondary studies (Hui et al., Waseem et al., Ghani et al., Fischer et al., Simosa and Siqueira) compared qualitatively
key_findings: System testing dominates (47), then integration 21, unit 15, acceptance 5; conformance 23, regression 14, API 8; performance 21, reliability 14, flexibility 2; specification-based strategies dominate; mostly lab experiments at TRL 3-4 and black-box; TrainTicket de-facto large SUT (16 studies), no standard small/medium MSA; no study directly addresses MSA security testing
author_limitations: Google Scholar reproducibility risk; peer-reviewed literature only (no white/grey literature); observer bias mitigated by kappa and joint discussion
analyst_limitations: Title-only query likely undercounts API testing (8) and misses REST API security work (P012, P014, P015) behind the 'no security testing' claim; small count inconsistencies (56+21 vs 74; duplicate arithmetic; 50/74 reported as 63%); no discussion of specification quality although specification-based strategies dominate
reproducibility: High: Zenodo replication package with selection, extraction data and code
suggested_extensions: Microservice API security testing (BOLA/authorization across services); spec-quality-aware conformance testing and failure attribution on TrainTicket-like systems; standard small/medium MSA benchmarks; updated mapping linking REST fuzzing literature
evidence_location: Identity p.1; related work p.3; search/selection p.3-4; extraction p.5; API testing p.7; results p.9-11; threats p.12; future directions p.13
integrity: Correct document (author-hosted IST version) replaces the earlier Ghani 2019 substitute; section order partly scrambled by two-column layout; tables column-split and figures missing; numbers taken from text
